newsitem.title: CANADA: Small Canadian gold stocks plummet on Bre-X news.
newsitem.headline: Small Canadian gold stocks plummet on Bre-X news.

text.p: Shares in small Canadian gold miners, especially those with Indonesian projects, fell sharply in early trading on Monday after news that Bre-X Minerals Ltd's 's claim of a huge Indonesia gold find was based on falsified data.

"I would not be surprised to see them trade down to what their cash value is, what kind of cash they have on hand. That is not a rational process, but that's the process that at least in the short-term may come to pass," said Gordon Capital analyst Barry Allen. He said investors would view unproven discoveries by Canadian prospectors with a healthy cynicism.

"There is an irrational process that will occur...as much as it went on the high side, it will now go to the negative side...it's like zero-based accounting, to a certain extent. Everyone will go back and re-value and re-look at everything, starting from the ground up," said Allen.

Trading of Bre-X and Minorca Resources Inc, which had a royalty interest in the Busang property, was halted at Monday's open, but other Canadian miners with Indonesian projects were hit by heavy selling. Scorpion Minerals Inc, with stakes in five Indonesian properties, fell 1.10 to 1.80 in busy trade.

Indomin Resources Ltd fell 1.08 to 1.90 on turnover of more than 280,000 shares. Indomin holds the rights to acquire several exploration interests in Indonesia, including an 85 percent stake in the 127,644-hectare Busang North gold property near the tainted Bre-X deposit.

Indochina Goldfields Ltd shares were also hit by the selloff, dropping 1 to 12 in moderate early trade. Shares in Mispec Resource Inc, which has mineral prospects in Indonesia as well as Atlantic Canada, recovered after opening down 1.00 at 1.00 to trade down 0.35 at 1.65 in healthy early trade.
International Pursuit Corp, which has properties in Indonesia, the Philippines, New Guinea and Canada's Yukon, fell 0.40 to 3 on more than 350,000 shares.
Allen said investors would view small miners and exploration firms and any new discoveries with a cynical eye after the Bre-X scandal.

"I think 'potential' or 'encouraging' or 'interesting' are all words which will not carry any meaningful value. And that will be the case until someone actually demonstrates there is a property of very significant merit," Allen said.

Allen said juniors would also be hurt in the long term as regulations are tightened after Bre-X, with exploration costs swelling as companies are forced to repeat drilling programs and conduct independent evaluations to meet new standards.
"It will be another sort of shoe that falls in the future, but it is something that people must have, should have on their minds. And it will be a good step, not a bad step," Allen said.
At the other end of the spectrum, Canada's major gold miners were boosted and the price of gold ticked up after the revelations that Bre-X would not be adding to world gold supply after all.

"The gold price is up a little bit this morning. I guess some of the scuttlebutt is the fact that there appears to be 71 million ounces (of gold) less than people had thought," said Research Capital Corp analysts Manford Mallory.
Shares in Barrick Gold Corp rose 0.50 to 31.90 in turnover of more than two million shares, while Placer Dome Inc rose 0.70 to 23.95 in heavy trade.
